scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Jikey is a secular Malay dance drama popular in the northern Peninsular states of Kedah and Perlis, with related traditions extending into Satun and Phuket in Thailand, as well as Cambodia.
It is believed to have developed after the late 19th century from the chanting of zikir, an Islamic devotional practice, before gradually evolving into a secular theatrical art form.
on_screen: Map: Malaysia · Southeast Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Jikey acts as popular community entertainment, drawing from local legends for its core repertoire.
It prioritizes comedic performance and slapstick humor to engage audiences, turning sacred devotional roots into accessible secular theatre.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music in Jikey plays a key role in identifying characters through leitmotifs.

A full Jikey orchestra consists of large, medium, and small rebana frame drums without jingles, one tambourine, one hanging knobbed gong, five or more pairs of cerek bamboo stampers, one pair of kesi cymbals, and a double-reed oboe (serunai in Malay or pi in Thai).
Listen for the rebana, tambourine, gong, cerek.

Melodic lines from a violin or serunai oboe lead the performance over a rhythmic foundation of layered rebana frame drums and clacking bamboo cerek stampers, supporting vocal dialogue and character leitmotifs.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Jikey forms part of a shared Southeast Asian theatrical tradition.
Rooted in Islamic zikir chanting, Jikey belongs to the broader Malay secular theatre family, maintaining strong artistic ties to Mak Yong, Bangsawan, Hadrah, and Mek Mulung.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Jikey is variant of Likay: Thai regional variant of the Jikey dance drama tradition.
Jikey is variant of Yike: Cambodian variant of the Jikey dance drama tradition.
Jikey is influence of Mak Yong: Traditional Malay performing art that influenced Jikey.
Jikey is influence of Bangsawan: Malay theatre form that influenced Jikey.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Jikey (Malaysia). Rhythm pattern: Rhythmic accompaniment driven by rebana frame drums and cerek bamboo stampers.. Instruments: rebana, tambourine, gong, cerek, kesi, serunai, violin. Vocal style: Vocal singing combined with improvised theatrical dialogue.. Form: Leitmotif system where dramatic characters are identified with specific musical elements.. Mood: comedic, theatrical, lively, dramatic. It should sound like this: Melodic lines from a violin or serunai oboe lead the performance over a rhythmic foundation of layered rebana frame drums and clacking bamboo cerek stampers, supporting vocal dialogue and character leitmotifs. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.
